solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Principal source of illness among crew

indicators.note: among says one piece sits inside the other, the illness letter amid the crew

parts.note: to crew a ship is to man it, so crew gives MAN

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, so take its opening letter

explanation.surface: Sickness aboard ship started mainly with the sailors themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Main and principal both mean chief or most important, as in the main road.

clue.text: A trial resulting in the rope

indicators.note: the letters of the first words turn into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A court case ends with someone facing the noose.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a long rope with a running noose, a lasso used by cowboys.

clue.text: Meet up and force argument

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for meet is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: meet as an adjective means proper or suitable, so FIT
F is the standard abbreviation for force in physics

explanation.surface: A get-together where pressure is applied ends in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a petty quarrel, a minor argument between friends or partners.

clue.text: Attack a vessel having trouble

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a vessel
to ail is to be unwell or have trouble

explanation.surface: Pirates storm a ship that is already in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack violently, physically or with words.

clue.text: Administrators are reportedly bound to look up

indicators.note: reportedly says a word is heard, so it is spelt by its sound

parts.note: bound means tied up, trussed, which sounds the same as TRUST

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for look is read backwards

parts.note: to look is to see

explanation.surface: Managers seem destined to examine the accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns TRUSSED into TRUST by sound; 'up' turns SEE into EES.
explanation.definitionFit: Trustees administer an estate, fund or charity on behalf of others.

clue.text: Taking no notice of little girl's message

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name (short for Diana), with the possessive S
a missive is a letter or message

explanation.surface: A short note from a young girl was waved aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dismissive means brushing something aside and paying it no attention.

clue.text: Food taken from a car on impulse

indicators.note: taken from the run of words means lifted out of them, letters spanning several words

explanation.surface: Someone grabbed a snack from the car on a whim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken' is the indicator and 'from' supplies the M: froM A CAR ON Impulse.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni is a pasta of narrow tubes, a staple food.

clue.text: Revealing the point of excursions

parts.note: outing someone is revealing a secret about them
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Explaining the purpose of day trips.
explanation.definitionFit: Outings are trips or excursions for pleasure.

clue.text: Mark's about right, it's stress!

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the mark goes round the letter for right

parts.note: a stain is a mark; the 's stands for is, a link

explanation.surface: A blemish on the right side causes anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: Strain and stress both mean pressure or tension, mental or physical.

clue.text: Take a firm stand at home and start to shave first

parts.note: being in means at home

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: 1st, read as IST, is a written form of first

explanation.surface: Be resolute at home and get the shaving done before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is not an order of work: written 1ST it reads IST.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to hold firmly to a demand or position, refusing to back down.

clue.text: Dreadful bowling of seamer

indicators.note: bowling suggests the letters are sent spinning into a new order

explanation.surface: A fast bowler's terrible spell in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: A seamer is a cricket bowler who makes the ball move off its seam.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearsome means frightening or dreadful.

clue.text: Do they see lots of bank clerks chasing great wealth?

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the clerks follow the wealth

parts.note: a fortune is a great deal of money
tellers are clerks who handle cash at a bank counter

explanation.surface: Bank staff pursue riches, but can they foresee much?
explanation.definitionFit: Fortune tellers claim to see what is in store, i.e. people's lots in life.

clue.text: Start to add flavour to food at this time of year

parts.note: to open is to start
to season food is to add salt, spice and so on

explanation.surface: Cooks begin spicing their dishes at this time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: Open season is the period when hunting a given game animal is permitted.

clue.text: Catch up — nothing right, but get the drift

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for catch is read backwards

parts.note: to net a fish is to catch it
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to keep pace with a conversation but understands its gist.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenor of a speech is its general sense or drift.

clue.text: Provide something to eat, but charge daughter

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

explanation.surface: A parent serves up a meal but bills their daughter for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To feed is to give someone food.

clue.text: Thai bride furiously excluded hotel in angry harangue

indicators.note: furiously suggests wild movement, so the letters are thrown into a new order
excluded means left out, so the hotel letter is removed

parts.note: Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A bride from Thailand, turned away from her hotel, rants furiously.
explanation.walkthrough: THAI BRIDE rearranged, with the H dropped, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a forceful denunciation.

clue.text: Ruling on issue of noise

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the other piece

parts.note: issue means offspring, such as a son
ruling means in charge, abbreviated IC

explanation.surface: A court judgment about a matter of disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic means relating to sound or noise.

clue.text: Vehicle with zero purpose except to have great fun

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
O looks like zero
use is purpose, as in what is the use of it

explanation.surface: A car with no point at all except for joyriding.
explanation.definitionFit: To carouse is to drink and make merry noisily.

clue.text: Prison unrest

explanation.definitionFit: Stir is slang for prison and also means a commotion or public excitement.

clue.text: Arrangement of terrace isn't bad, but makes you dizzy

indicators.note: an arrangement of letters puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: Badly laid-out garden terracing gives a visitor vertigo.
explanation.definitionFit: Dizzy in its informal sense means silly or flighty, like a scatterbrain.

clue.text: Changed course due to report of diplomacy

indicators.note: a report is what is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: tact is diplomacy, skill in handling people

explanation.surface: A government shifted policy because of a diplomatic dispatch.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing ship that tacked turned into the wind to change course.

clue.text: Units deployed to support one are correctly positioned

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting below the other piece

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: troops deployed are spread out and rearranged

explanation.surface: Army units are sent to back up a single soldier in place.
explanation.definitionFit: In situ is Latin for in its original or proper place.

clue.text: Provides accommodation for lawyers with instruments of torture

parts.note: the Bar is the body of barristers, lawyers
racks are frames for stretching victims

explanation.surface: A grim lodging for the legal profession, furnished with torture racks.
explanation.definitionFit: To barrack troops is to house them in barracks, giving them lodging.

clue.text: Location? Listen to sense

indicators.note: listening means the word is taken by how it is heard

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: Someone asks where to go and is told to be reasonable.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a place or location, as in a building site.

clue.text: Disappointments experienced by leading groups

parts.note: up means ahead, leading, as in two goals up
sets are groups

explanation.surface: Teams at the top of the table suffer setbacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Upsets are unexpected reverses or disappointments.

clue.text: Ship's movement makes you throw up!

definitions.meaning: a ship ... as it pitches in rough seas
to throw something upwards, like a coin

explanation.definitionFit: Toss means both a pitching motion of a vessel and to fling into the air.

clue.text: Gloomy and painful around the doctor

indicators.note: around means the painful word encloses the doctor

parts.note: sore means painful
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Feeling miserable and aching while waiting for the GP.
explanation.definitionFit: Sombre means dark and gloomy in mood or colour.

clue.text: Deal with single case of scrapie in critical analysis

parts.note: to treat a problem is to deal with it
I, the Roman numeral one, means single

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, first and last letters

explanation.surface: Vets handle a lone outbreak of a sheep disease and write it up.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrapie is a brain disease of sheep; 'case of' gives its first and last letters, SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written study analysing a subject in depth.
